final_message:
I reproduced the bug at c1caacd. When the browser navigates to `/test`, the dev server sends back `test.js` as `text/javascript` instead of `index.html`. I haven't changed any source code; I only added a failing test and a small fixture (`index.html`, `main.js`, `test.js`, and no `test.html`).

Run from the repo root: `pnpm vitest run packages/vite/src/node/server/__tests__/htmlFallbackSourceFile.spec.ts`

The test sends the headers a browser uses when you click a link (`Accept: text/html,...`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`, `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`). It has two cases, and both fail on current main:
- **Fresh server:** `GET /test` returns `text/javascript` containing `export const marker = 'TEST_JS'`.
- **After `/`, `/main.js` and `/test.js` have already been loaded:** you get the same JS response.

I ran the same check against the published releases:

| version | fresh `/test` | after test.js is loaded |
|---|---|---|
| 7.0.4 | index.html | **test.js** |
| 7.0.5 | **test.js** | **test.js** |

What the code shows:
- **The change that caused it:** commit c9614b9, "fix: remove special handling for `Accept: text/html` (#20376)". It stopped passing `html: req.headers.accept?.includes('text/html')` from `transformMiddleware` into `transformRequest`. It also dropped the early `if (options.html && !id.endsWith('.html')) return null` and the `html:`-prefixed pending-request key.
- **Why `/test` counts as a JS request:** `isJSRequest()` treats any path with no file extension as JS. Then `transformRequest` resolves `/test` to `test.js`, so `transformMiddleware` answers before `htmlFallbackMiddleware`/`indexHtmlMiddleware` get a chance.
- **The second case also fails on 7.0.4.** A request that repeats the module's etag in `If-None-Match` would be answered by `cachedTransformMiddleware` before the transform step, and that middleware never looked at `Accept`. That fits the maintainer's comment about the second visit. But I haven't confirmed that's what causes my warm-case failure: `fetch` doesn't send `If-None-Match` unless you set it, and my second case doesn't. Either way, bringing back the removed check alone probably won't fix both cases.

The patch contains only the test and the fixture files.

fetch(`${baseUrl}/main.js`)).text() + await (await fetch(`${baseUrl}/test.js`)).text() + + const res = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/test`, { headers: navigationHeaders }) + const body = await res.text() + console.log( + `[warm] GET /test -> ${res.status} content-type=${res.headers.get('content-type')}\n${body.slice(0, 200)}`, + ) + expect(res.headers.get('content-type')).toMatch(/text\/html/) + expect(body).toContain('INDEX_HTML') + expect(body).not.toContain('TEST_JS') + }) +})
